transcript_window.text: David, we appreciate you.
Is the route to making college football this celestial product, right?
Is the path through federal legislation and the federal government intervening to help govern it?
Or is it through what I would deem the university saying, you know what, we need to take a little bit more accountability.
Maybe it's within the conferences, but the universities have to say, you know what, we're going to employ, you know, help execute and facilitate a players' union, right?
We're going to help quarterback this within the power structure and then, you know, allow them to, you know, collectively bargain.
Morgan, you know, those are the two routes that I see.
And it's either the university is going to say we're going to take the baton or we're going to just sit there at the doorstep of the federal government.
Which path do you think is better?
There are a lot smarter people than me trying to figure this out.
But my opinion is, you know, it's a little bit when you look at the NCAA and for decades and decades and people want to criticize the NCAA.
Why did they do this?
Why did they do this?
And I always want to point out the NCAA is its member institutions.
It's not a monolith that's making these decisions on its own.
So I think there's a little parallel there.
People don't realize that.
Right.
And so you look at college football and you say, can we govern ourselves without the help of a federal intervention?

And my hope is that not the threat, but the potential of federal intervention will cause all of the parties at the table to say, look, do we want to control our own destiny or do we want to allow governmental influence to make decisions for us?
Yeah, it's my hope.
And this is just a guy saying that I think a guy that's been in it for 32 years and been seen a lot, done a lot.
True.

It's my hope that the college football leadership can say, let's govern ourselves and come up with a model that works, is fair enough for everybody, and we can put our self -interest aside just a little bit, enough so that we can keep it within a tighter circle and we don't have to have federal intervention.

I think that speaks to your background and how you've operated the Chick -fil -A Bowl, the charitable, the synergy, the entrepreneur, the incentive -based structure in order to get everybody together to see the vision.
